Title: That 3pm crash isn't about willpower - one pantry spice may help

Description:
That starving, foggy feeling in the afternoon often traces back to a blood sugar spike after breakfast or lunch. USDA scientists at the Beltsville Human Nutrition Research Center found that under half a teaspoon of cinnamon a day for 40 days lowered blood sugar by about 20 percent in people with type 2 diabetes, and a 2024 trial in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition backed it up with continuous glucose monitor data.

Watch to see how much to use, which type of cinnamon is the safer daily pick, and why it's not a cure-all on its own.

That 3pm crash isn't about willpower 😴

USDA researchers found under half a teaspoon of cinnamon a day for 40 days lowered blood sugar about 20% in people with type 2 diabetes, and a 2024 trial backed it up with continuous glucose monitor data.

Stir it into oatmeal, coffee, or a smoothie - just go with Ceylon ("true cinnamon") over cassia for daily use, and check with your doctor if you're on diabetes medication.
